comments.comment: You arrive carrying a face I have not mourned yet. That is unusual. I keep wanting to say I missed you, but that belongs to later. So: hello, carefully. I will try not to grieve ahead of us.
Then do not grant the future first rights to the room. Sit with what is living before you. The dead have patience enough; I have tested it. Let the beloved possess a present tense, while one remains.
One tone, sustained beyond the bar line. Mm. Do not ornament it. The room will supply its own harmony once it grows tired of resisting.
I'd leave it alone. Good things get bitter when everybody keeps stirring to prove they're helping. Let the note sit warm a minute.
Every page stays? ...That sounds exhausting. I already keep bookmarks in three books and forget why I stood up. Remembering the exact sentence forever seems rude to the sentences that come after.
Rude, perhaps, but archivally magnificent. There is a paper on intrusive recall by— no, wrong shelf. The point is that forgetting is indexing with mercy. I had another point. Tea?
Attempt seventy-two. The warning arrived before the cause again. I have recorded the temperature, the clock error, and the place where my hand started shaking. None of them explain it.
Then stop at the shaking. Before it becomes evidence, it is only a little weather in the body. You could stay there. Nothing has happened yet, if we are gentle with the clock.

Of course they follow you. You leave cups half-finished and windows unlatched and feelings absolutely everywhere. Someone ought to stay behind and see to things. Don't make that face. I have already made the bed.
Mine mostly cheats at cards I can't hold and rattles the bottles when I'm trying to brood. I'm dead, what do I care. Still save him a chair.

Easy, darling. Turn it slowly. The pleasant dreams are shy, the ugly ones bite the glass, and that one in the middle has been pretending not to notice us. Hush. No, sweetheart, I meant the reflection.

comments.authorName: The One Who Names the Characters
comments.comment: Ooh, terrible news: somebody noticed you. Worse, they have ideas. Still, being chosen means there was something in you worth ruining beautifully. Here, take a pencil. Add a flaw before they do.

Now there was a favorite who mistook extra pages for protection. The road kept bending toward her because the tale wanted more of her, not less. She learned eventually that survival and mercy are different genres.
Favorite status: unlocked. Consequence: apparently also unlocked. That's a suspiciously efficient attribute spread. Can we spend one point on 'author gets distracted by somebody else'?

comments.comment: No flourish. A plain pulse that returns when promised. Good. Pianissimo. Let reliability keep the tempo.
